issues.description: Exercise 3's oracle method is declared to accept a single string in the template (combinations: str), while the problem statement and the solution expect a list of bit-strings (list[str]). This mismatch between the template signature and the intended usage (and the grover_circuit which expects list[str]) will confuse students and break their implementations when they try to call oracle with a list of combinations as described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature for oracle to accept a list of strings (combinations: list[str]) to match the problem statement and the solution. Ensure any references and docstrings are consistent and that grover_circuit and run pass a list of bit-strings accordingly.

issues.description: The conceptual entity representing multiple target bit-strings for Exercise 3 is described and used as a list of strings in the problem statement and in the solution implementation, but the template's oracle function signature accepts a single string (type annotation 'str'). This mismatch of the 'combinations' parameter type in the template (str) versus the problem statement and solution (list[str]) creates confusion about whether the oracle should handle one combination or multiple combinations and may mislead students when implementing or testing the oracle.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template oracle function signature to accept the same conceptual type as the problem statement and solution (use parameter type list[str], e.g. def oracle(..., combinations: list[str], ...) ) and adjust the docstring to indicate it handles multiple bit-strings. This aligns template, problem text, and solution and removes ambiguity for students.
